_comment: The A0 latency baseline, as DATA. It has lived in the ledger as a markdown
table since 2026-08-20, which is fine to read and impossible to compare
against without a person retyping numbers. C4 is exactly that comparison,
so the numbers move here and the ledger table stays as the narrative.
RECORD HERE, NEVER OVERWRITE. A baseline that gets updated to match the
current deployment is not a baseline. If the target changes, add a second
file; do not edit this one.
_platformCaveat: A0 ran on RAILWAY, reached through carrier hops from a real handset.
Everything C4 compares it against runs on Cloud Run. End-to-end numbers
are therefore not strictly comparable and a delta on them is partly the
The per-STAGE numbers are server-side and measured inside one process, so
they are comparable. That distinction is not pedantry: it is what let the
TTS finding stand up — tts_ttfb_ms 92 -> 1,408 ms is a server-side stage
and 15x is not a carrier artefact.

endToEnd._note: Not strictly comparable across platforms. Read the deltas as indicative.

stages._note: Server-side, single process. These are the comparable numbers.

llm_ttfb_ms.note: 42% of the turn at A0 — the dominant stage

llm_tool_ms.note: null on turns with no tool call — metrics.js says so in its own comment. Absence is normal, not a finding.

tts_ttfb_ms.note: At A0, TTS was not a latency problem. On the covered lane it is the largest single regression.

turnsTimedOutNoReply.note: Predates the migration and is not fixed by it. Recorded so it cannot be misattributed to the migration, and because it is the thing a clinic notices first.
